clue.text: Bigoted, as some books might be

definitions.meaning: narrow-minded and set in rigid opinions
literally, a volume whose covers are made of leather from an animal's skin

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, old volumes bound in leather skins; figuratively, a person cramped by convention and prejudice.

clue.text: Feverishly impetuous?

parts.note: a feverish person has a high temperature in the skull, which also describes someone rash

explanation.definitionFit: Literally having a high temperature in the skull; idiomatically rash and quick-tempered.

clue.text: Ventured to see king in late rising

indicators.note: the king goes inside the other piece
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late Mr Smith
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Took a chance on visiting the monarch as he got up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns DEAD into DAED, and 'in' puts R inside it; 'to see' is a joining phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare is to have the nerve to try something, so dared means took the risk.

clue.text: Bronte of note — won the sprint?

parts.note: B is a musical note
a winning sprinter ran well

explanation.surface: Which famous literary sibling was the athlete of the family?
explanation.walkthrough: Branwell was the brother of Charlotte, Emily and Anne Bronte; 'of' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick Branwell, painter and poet, was the only brother of the novelist sisters.

clue.text: Sort of income of a foreign composer, many conclude

parts.note: une is French for a
Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A kind of earnings from an overseas composer, many decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclude' signals that D comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Income from investments rather than work, such as dividends, is classed as unearned.

clue.text: Saying appears obscure about, TUC members

indicators.note: the dim piece goes round the other letters

parts.note: dim means obscure, unclear

indicators.note: the members of the union initials are taken in a different order

explanation.surface: A statement seems vague regarding trade union members.
explanation.walkthrough: TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's union federation; 'members' shuffles its letters to CTU, which goes inside DIM; 'appears' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pronouncement or maxim is a dictum, a synonym for a saying.

clue.text: Church notes taken by the president

parts.note: musical notes strung together make a tune or melody, an air

explanation.surface: Hymn music being performed in the presence of a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by the' merely joins the pieces to the definition; the president here is whoever presides over a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting's presiding officer is addressed as its chair, a synonym for the one who presides.

clue.text: Cast me in Buffalo Bill play

indicators.note: to cast an actor is to put them into a role, so this pairs with in to signal placing inside
together with cast, this places the speaker inside the showman's surname

parts.note: William Cody, the American showman

explanation.surface: A request to be given a part in a Wild West show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast ... in' looks like an anagram signal but means place inside: ME goes into CODY, unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-hearted drama is a comedy, one kind of play.

clue.text: RAF type demanded to be applauded

parts.note: AC, aircraftman, is a rank in the Royal Air Force
claimed means demanded as a right

explanation.surface: An airman insisted on being cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a joining phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hailed with praise and cheering is to be acclaimed.

clue.text: Annoyed and upset doctor about priest

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards
the doctor goes round the priest

parts.note: Eli was the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Irritated, a distressed physician turns on the cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ELI inside DR to give DELIR, which 'upset' turns over; 'and' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means irritated or made angry, a synonym for annoyed.

clue.text: The row the builders made

parts.note: reads like noise from a building site, but a row here is a line of joined houses that builders erected

explanation.definitionFit: A British name for a street of houses joined in one continuous block, built as a single row.

clue.text: Firm gets claim for replacement — that's funny

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the letters of claim are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A company submits an insurance claim for new goods, and someone finds it amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' rearranges CLAIM into MICAL, which follows CO; 'gets' and 'that's' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laughable or amusing is described as comical, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Present carried by Glendower

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the name Glendower, sitting within it

explanation.surface: A gift borne by Owen Glendower, the Welsh rebel prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Owain Glyndwr (Glendower), a Welsh rebel leader who appears in Shakespeare's Henry IV; 'Present' is the verb, to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow funds or a gift on someone, as in giving money to an institution, is a verb sense of present.

clue.text: Style of writing from canon to worker

parts.note: a canon in music is a round, a song where voices enter in turn
a hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A cleric's script passed along to a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' suggests a churchman, but it is the musical canon; 'from ... to' just leads one piece onto the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold, rounded penmanship style once taught to clerks is called roundhand.

clue.text: Revealed guile, five sorts, in a theologian

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit within the theologian's abbreviation

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by a theologian

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A divine confessed to cunning, sorted into five kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorts' rearranges GUILE plus V into IVULGE, which goes 'in' DD.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose a secret is to make it known, the sense of revealed.

clue.text: Green coat for composer — gray when abroad

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
gris is French for gray

explanation.surface: A green jacket for a musician, which looks grey overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: The green patina that forms on copper and bronze is verdigris, a coating.

clue.text: Send out East German with joiner

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
the joining word with is mit in German

explanation.surface: Broadcasting a man from East Germany alongside a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter, but it describes 'with', a word that joins things.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off or discharge light, heat or a signal is to send it out.

clue.text: Act about new stake in an Asian region

indicators.note: the act goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A performance concerning a fresh bet placed in part of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes KESTA from STAKE, and 'about' puts TURN round it; 'in' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic Central Asian territory spanning modern Kazakhstan and Xinjiang, land of the Turkic peoples.

clue.text: Poet revised sonnet about the Empire State

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the state abbreviation
revising changes the order of the word's letters

parts.note: New York's nickname; NY is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A writer reworks a fourteen-line poem about New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' makes TENSON from SONNET, split 'about' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Might give one a ring when depressed

definitions.text: Might give one a ring when depressed

parts.words: Might give one a ring when depressed
parts.note: sounds like a gloomy friend phoning, but describes a device that rings when its button is pressed

explanation.definitionFit: A push-button device at the entrance chimes when pressed, summoning the householder.

clue.text: Boat supplies same transport

parts.note: DO, short for ditto, means the same again
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a form of transport

explanation.surface: A vessel provides the same kind of conveyance as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplies' just joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat-bottomed fishing vessel with high sides is a dory.

clue.text: Judicial type of instrument

definitions.meaning: a part-time judge in English courts holds this title
a wooden wind instrument played in schools

explanation.definitionFit: In England a barrister sitting part-time as a judge has this title; it is also an end-blown woodwind flute.

clue.text: A fabric supplied whenever one likes

parts.note: twill is a cloth with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Some cloth handed out as and when anyone fancies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning as and when one pleases, freely and without restriction.

clue.text: Writer appears happy (helping himself too?)

definitions.meaning: Samuel ..., Victorian author of the book Self-Help
beams with pleasure on the face

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hints at his best-known book, Self-Help.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Smiles wrote Self-Help, a Victorian bestseller; a person who grins looks pleased.

clue.text: Railway employee gives tips before the race

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the other

parts.note: points are tips, as of pencils or knives
mankind, the human race, is man

explanation.surface: A rail worker offers betting advice ahead of the horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' and 'race' suggest racing advice, but they are sharp ends and the human race; 'gives' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: On British railways the man who worked the switches between tracks was a pointsman.

clue.text: Cats in turn, get Pickwick's man out of bed

indicators.note: the whole assembled run is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: Felines in their turn rouse Mr Pickwick's servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses SAMUP; 'get' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Large American wild felines, also called cougars or mountain lions.

clue.text: Wood returns the foreign weapon

indicators.note: the word for wood is read back to front

parts.note: fir is a timber, a kind of wood
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone named Wood gives back a gun from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns FIR into RIF, before LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled gun fired from the shoulder is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Meeting of strikers, panic? Not right

indicators.note: not signals that the letter for right is left out

parts.note: fright is sudden fear or panic

explanation.surface: Union members on strike gather and wonder whether panic is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' suggests industrial action, but they are people who hit each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout between two people trading punches is a contest of strikers.

clue.text: Hawk-like Latin poet

definitions.meaning: warlike, as a political hawk favours war
the Roman epigrammatist of the first century AD

explanation.definitionFit: Warlike, like a political hawk; also the name of the Roman writer of epigrams.

clue.text: Old Bob gets £8 by a trick

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
the pound sign is L (from Latin libra) and 8 is spelt out

explanation.surface: An elderly man called Bob pockets eight pounds by deception.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is not a name but British slang for a shilling, written s; 'gets' and 'by a' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is deft conjuring, so sleight means a cunning trick or dexterity.

clue.text: Fibre returned by girl about one

indicators.note: the whole assembled piece is read backwards
the girl goes round the letter for one

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thread sent back by a young woman concerning one item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside LASS to give LASIS, and 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong plant fibre from agave leaves used for rope and matting is sisal.

clue.text: Card for, one fashion, assembly

indicators.note: the two pieces are assembled, put together side by side

parts.note: single means one
ton is an old word for fashion, high style

explanation.surface: A greeting card for one fashion gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, from French, means the fashionable set or style; 'for' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the lone card held in a suit is called a singleton.
